candidates.name: kraina/airbnb (mirror of Gyódi & Nawaro EU-cities dataset)
candidates.what_it_holds: 51.7k row Parquet dataset (25.5k weekday + 26.2k weekend offers) across 10 European cities (Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, London, Paris, Rome, Vienna), originally the supplementary data for Gyódi & Nawaro (2021) 'Determinants of Airbnb prices in European cities: A spatial econometrics approach', mirrored from Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.4446043) onto Hugging Face by the Kraina geospatial research group. Fields include price, room type, host status (superhost), ratings/review count, capacity, bedrooms, distance to center, and a TripAdvisor-based attractiveness index. CC-BY-4.0.
candidates.why_useful: A cross-sectional but multi-city (10 EU cities), academically-vetted realised-price dataset with weekday/weekend price splits — useful as an independent check on ADR/seasonality mix assumptions for EMEA, and the underlying Zenodo record + paper's methodology (spatial regression on price determinants) is a candidate replication package for the ADR decomposition workstream. Not new geography beyond what we hold (Paris, Barcelona, Rome overlap our 13-city panel) but adds Athens, Budapest, Lisbon, Vienna and a peer-reviewed price-driver framework.
candidates.geography: 10 EU cities (Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, London, Paris, Rome, Vienna)
candidates.time_coverage: single cross-sectional pull (~2018-2020 per paper vintage; exact scrape date not stated on HF page)
candidates.last_activity: Zenodo record published 2021; HF mirror undated
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partial overlap in geography with our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel (Paris, Barcelona, Rome) but different data source/vintage and includes weekday/weekend price split we do not have

candidates.name: tmasjc/airbnb-market-data
candidates.what_it_holds: R/Shiny dashboard shipping committed Inside Airbnb listings.csv summary files for Berlin and Vienna, plus a CLI tool (download_csv.R) that can list ALL Inside Airbnb cities and, critically, list and fetch HISTORICAL SNAPSHOTS BY DATE INDEX for a given city (`./download_csv.R list -s {city}` shows a dated snapshot index; `-i <index>` pulls an older vintage). Vienna sample data shown dates to Sep 2017-Mar 2017.
candidates.why_useful: The CLI's historical-snapshot indexing is a possible mechanism for pulling Inside Airbnb vintages older than the ~1-year CDN retention window we're currently limited to (2017-era snapshots referenced) — directly relevant to gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps, pre-2023, including the NYC Local-Law-18 gap window). Needs verification of what host download_csv.R actually hits (may just be pointing at Wayback-cached Inside Airbnb URLs).
candidates.geography: Any Inside Airbnb city (Berlin, Vienna committed as samples)
candidates.time_coverage: Tool can reach snapshots at least back to 2017 per README example
candidates.size_hint: Small committed CSVs (2 cities); tool is unbounded

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Python + PostgreSQL/PostGIS scraper (bounding-box, neighborhood, or zipcode search) for Airbnb listing data. No committed data files or release assets — tool only. Author (Tom Slee), whose historical 2015-2017 Airbnb scrapes predate and partly inspired Inside Airbnb, states he is no longer maintaining it and is looking for a new owner. MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Named author's original historical city-level Airbnb scrapes (2014-2017, dozens of cities, pre-dating Inside Airbnb's own coverage) are a known historical dataset in the STR-data literature; this repo is the associated tooling, not the data itself — worth checking Tom Slee's personal site/blog (airbnbdata.com, now defunct per other search hits) or Wayback Machine for the actual archived CSVs it produced, which would fill gap #1 for years before Inside Airbnb existed.
candidates.geography: Configurable, any city (historically dozens of cities scraped by the author 2014-2017)
candidates.time_coverage: Tool is current; author's own historical runs were 2014-2017

candidates.name: luminati-io/Airbnb-dataset-samples (Bright Data)
candidates.what_it_holds: airbnb-properties-information.csv with 1,001 sample rows drawn from a larger Bright Data commercial dataset described as covering 'more than 11,000,000' Airbnb-adjacent records; fields include property id/name/url, price, location/coordinates, guest capacity, host info, amenities, availability dates, ratings/reviews. Full dataset obtainable (paid) via Bright Data API on a custom refresh cadence (once/daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly).
candidates.why_useful: A commercially-scraped, apparently current, very large-scale Airbnb listings dataset (11M+ full size) exists behind Bright Data's paid API; the free sample is small (1,001 rows, no stated cities/years) but flags that a paid, current, global Airbnb listing feed is available if the team ever wants pricing/availability at a scale beyond Inside Airbnb. Scraping airbnb.com — per our rules this is a human ToS decision, not something to run ourselves.
candidates.size_hint: 1,001-row free sample; 11M+ row paid dataset claimed

candidates.name: airbert-vln/bnb-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic (vision-and-language navigation research) tooling to scrape Airbnb listing photos and captions (TSV format: listing ID, photo ID, image URL, caption), generated Christmas 2019, filtered to indoor photos via a Places365 CNN classifier, with LMDB feature extraction pipeline. Repo provides only the download/processing scripts, not a redistributable image dataset, due to Airbnb IP restrictions on images.
candidates.why_useful: Not directly useful for KPI forecasting (image/caption data, not price or nights) but documents a working, non-trivial Airbnb-listing scraper built for an academic paper (used for indoor-scene research) — low relevance to ABNB thesis, flagged mainly to rule out as a source.
candidates.geography: multiple cities via Wikipedia-seeded location list, unspecified count
candidates.license: MIT (code); no redistribution rights on Airbnb images

candidates.name: dtrungtin/actor-airbnb-scraper (Apify actor)
candidates.what_it_holds: An Apify 'actor' (packaged scraper) that extracts publicly available Airbnb listing search results and detail pages for any area, outputting JSON/CSV/XML/RSS/HTML Table via the Apify platform's dataset export. No committed data, tool/method only.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, currently-listed (GitHub topics surfaced it with April-2026-era activity referenced) scraper-as-a-service for Airbnb — same category as Bright Data: a live scraper of airbnb.com, which is explicitly a ToS decision for a human under our rules, not something to run. Catalogued as method only, unrun.
candidates.last_activity: topic page suggests recent (2026) activity in this space

candidates.name: Zenodo: Determinants of Airbnb prices in European cities (supplementary data)
candidates.what_it_holds: Original Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4446043) for the Gyódi & Nawaro paper: per-city weekday/weekend CSVs for 10 EU cities plus the Python spatial-econometrics replication scripts (not just the flat data — includes the modeling code).
candidates.why_useful: This is the authoritative source behind the kraina/HF and multiple GitHub mirrors above; unlike the mirrors, it also ships the actual spatial-regression replication code, which is a genuine academic replication package (methods) for price-determinant modeling, relevant to the ADR decomposition workstream (methods gap #17 adjacent).
candidates.license: not explicitly stated on page (paper is Elsevier; supplementary data typically CC-BY)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Source dataset for kraina/airbnb, BercinErsoz, and OludolapoAnalyst GitHub mirrors above

notes: This theme is heavily saturated with single-city, single-vintage 'Airbnb price prediction' student/tutorial repos built on either the well-known Kaggle AB_NYC_2019 file or the Seattle/Boston 2016 Kaggle set — these were excluded per instructions as they add nothing new. The one genuinely distinct multi-city cross-sectional dataset that recurs across many independent GitHub mirrors is the Gyódi & Nawaro 10-European-city weekday/weekend dataset (Zenodo record 4446043, mirrored to Hugging Face by kraina, and copied into at least 3 separate GitHub repos found here) — flagged once at the Zenodo/HF level as the canonical source, with the GitHub mirrors noted as low-value duplicates. The two most operationally interesting finds are tmasjc/airbnb-market-data's historical-snapshot-by-date-index CLI (possible route to pre-2023 Inside Airbnb vintages, gap #1) and tomslee/airbnb-data-collection (the tooling behind a known pre-Inside-Airbnb historical scrape lineage, also gap #1) — both need a follow-up fetch/run-through by a human or a dedicated agent to confirm they actually reach older data rather than just erroring against the current live site. No large *multi-year* committed listings archive (i.e., many repeated snapshots of the same cities over multiple years, all committed as data files rather than pulled live) turned up in this pass beyond the small Christchurch student project (excluded, too small/recent to matter) — if another scout is assigned a second pass on this theme, searching GitHub Releases pages directly (assets, not repo file listings) and Kaggle's own API-linked GitHub companion repos would be the next places to look. No dead ends beyond ordinary search noise; no rate-limit issues encountered.
